chunks: And from him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban, from Zakkar ibn Farqad, from Uthman ibn Ziyad — he said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): I am on a journey and come to stagnant water while my hands are dirty, then I submerge them in the water.
He said: There is no harm.

key_terms.الْمَاءَ النَّقِيعَ: stagnant/pooled water — a body of standing water encountered during travel; the root n-q-' also yields nabidh (date-infused water), but the tahara context favors standing/collected water
key_terms.قَذِرَةٌ: dirty/impure — hands in a state of physical dirt or ritual najasah
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: no harm — the standard Imami jurisprudential formula declaring an act permissible

ai.seo_question: Does immersing dirty hands in stagnant water during travel make it ritually impure according to Imam al-Baqir (AS)?
ai.summary: Uthman ibn Ziyad asked Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) whether submerging dirty (ritually impure) hands into stagnant water during travel is permissible. The Imam's reply of 'lā ba's' (no harm) is a standard jurisprudential formula of permissibility, implying that the water does not thereby become ritually impure — a ruling relevant to the chapter's theme of small quantities of water and najasah.
word_analysis: I am / I happen to be
